question: The average of first 170 even numbers is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of the first n even numbers is directly given by the formula (n + 1).

Here, the number of terms n = 170.

⇒ Average = 170 + 1 = 171

**∴ The correct answer is 171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = 170

The sequence of the first 170 even numbers is: 2, 4, 6, ..., 340

**Formula Used:**

Average of an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 
•

 2
 4
 6
 . . . . . . .

 Average = (2 + 340) ÷ 2 = 171
 First 170 Even Numbers

**Calculations:**

⇒ First term (a) = 2

⇒ Last term (l) = 170 × 2 = 340

⇒ Average = (2 + 340) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 342 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 171

**∴ The correct answer is 171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of first n natural numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is calculated using the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of first n odd numbers

The average of the first n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is exactly equal to n.

Average of an Arithmetic Progression

For any given sequence of numbers that maintains a constant difference between consecutive terms, the average is strictly derived by (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.
